text:
My friend @harrisonjaime is one of the best leaders & did extraordinary work in building a multiracial coalition that opened many doors for people like me who, as an Indian American of Hindu faith, never had a shot in politics growing up. 

My friend @davidsirota is passionate about the party returning to our roots of fighting for the working class & standing against foreign wars.

If we can come together, which we will, we will build one of the greatest coalitions for progressive change since A. Philip Randolph and Bayard Rustin championed the Freedom budget.

Let's build a movement that can transform our nation.

That begins in November.

That is our duty and destiny.

quoted.text:
To what end, David? 

Congrats… you won your seat running against the “establishment.” Threw mud all over the party. Now what?

Can you pass a bill by yourself? Nope. 

Can you get your agenda through a Republican majority? Good luck. 

Want to win the White House? To get to 270, you’re going to need some of those same folks you keep shitting on.

Run your own race. Tell folks where you disagree. But there’s a difference between that and telling everybody the whole damn party is worthless.

If you win,  but other Democrats lose, who’s passing your agenda?! 

It is the collective that makes things happen in our government and not the individual.  You have to find a way to work with folks. 

Otherwise you’re slashing the tires on the same damn bus you need to get somewhere. Make it make sense.

Bottomline- save the fights for the primary.  Let’s all win in the general!

Three years ago today, Hamas carried out a horrific terrorist attack on Israel, killing 1,200 people and taking hundreds hostage. We remember those who were murdered, those who were taken from their families, and the survivors who still carry the trauma of that day. Since then, Palestinians have suffered horrifically at the hands of the Israeli government. To this day, there is unimaginable suffering in Gaza.

There has been too much death and too much grief. Israelis and Palestinians alike deserve to live in with security and dignity. We must keep working toward a lasting peace.
